title: Cross-Partition Transaction Overuse (2PC Bottlenecks)
pattern: Structuring distributed database schemas so that common, high-frequency transactions must cross multiple sharding partitions, triggering expensive distributed atomic commit protocols.
why_bad: Distributed transactions require Two-Phase Commit (2PC), which forces coordinator locks, blocking commits, and multiple network rounds across database sharding nodes. A single cross-partition write can be orders of magnitude slower than a single-partition write, creating a massive scalability bottleneck that cannot be solved by adding machines.
detection: Database access statements executing writes on sharding keys that map to different network nodes inside a single transaction boundary.
counterexample: Low-frequency operations (such as weekly balance reconciliations) where transactional accuracy overrides throughput.
source: *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 7, "Transactions" (Single-threaded serial transaction processing, p. 244 & Distributed Transactions, p. 254); *Alex Petrov - Database Internals (2019)*, Chapter 13.
